title: At Work - First Day
objectives: Ask for clarification politely at work
Describe your job duties and responsibilities
Talk about your work schedule and breaks
target_phrases: Could you show me how to...?
I'm not sure what to do next

dialogue.title: First Day at the Warehouse
dialogue.context: It's Ahmed's first day at his new warehouse job. His supervisor Tony shows him around and explains the job.

lines.speaker: Tony
lines.text: Good morning, Ahmed! Welcome to your first day. I'm Tony, your supervisor.

lines.speaker: Ahmed
lines.text: Good morning, Tony. Thank you! I'm excited to start.

lines.speaker: Tony
lines.text: Great! First, let me show you where to clock in. You need to scan your badge here every day.

lines.speaker: Ahmed
lines.text: Okay. What time should I arrive?

lines.speaker: Tony
lines.text: Your shift starts at 8 AM, but please arrive by 7:55 so you're ready to start on time.

lines.speaker: Ahmed
lines.text: Got it. And when is my lunch break?

lines.speaker: Tony
lines.text: You get a 30-minute lunch break at 12:00 PM. You also get two 15-minute breaks - one at 10 AM and one at 3 PM.

lines.speaker: Ahmed
lines.text: Thank you. What are my main responsibilities?

lines.speaker: Tony
lines.text: You'll be loading and unloading trucks, organizing inventory, and keeping the warehouse clean. Let me show you the loading area.

lines.speaker: Ahmed
lines.text: Could you show me how to use the forklift?

lines.speaker: Tony
lines.text: Not yet. First, you need to complete safety training tomorrow. Never use equipment without training.

lines.speaker: Ahmed
lines.text: I understand. Safety first. If I'm not sure what to do, should I ask you?

lines.speaker: Tony
lines.text: Yes, always ask if you're not sure. It's better to ask questions than make mistakes. I'm here to help!

listening_exercises.transcript: Welcome to orientation! Today we'll cover company policies. First, attendance: You must arrive on time for your shift. If you're going to be late or absent, call your supervisor at least 2 hours before your shift starts. Three unexcused absences may result in termination.
listening_exercises.question: What should you do if you will be late for work?

listening_exercises.transcript: Safety is our top priority. Always wear your safety gear - hard hat, safety vest, and steel-toed boots. Never operate machinery you haven't been trained on. If you see a safety hazard, report it immediately to your supervisor. We have safety meetings every Monday morning at 7:30 AM.
listening_exercises.question: What should you do if you see a safety hazard?
options: Report it to your supervisor immediately
Wait until the Monday safety meeting

listening_exercises.transcript: Your paycheck comes every two weeks on Friday. We use direct deposit - your money goes straight to your bank account. Make sure to give HR your bank information. You can check your hours and pay stubs online through the employee portal. If you have questions about your pay, contact the HR department.
listening_exercises.question: How often do employees get paid?

speaking_tasks.prompt: Imagine your supervisor asks: 'What are your main responsibilities?' Record yourself describing 3-4 job duties. Talk for at least 30 seconds.
speaking_tasks.example: I'm responsible for several things. First, I load and unload delivery trucks. Second, I organize inventory in the warehouse. Third, I keep my work area clean and safe. Finally, I help my coworkers when they need assistance.

speaking_tasks.prompt: Practice asking polite questions at work. Record yourself asking: 'Could you show me how to use the time clock?' and 'I'm not sure where the break room is. Could you help me?'
speaking_tasks.example: Excuse me, could you show me how to use the time clock? I want to make sure I'm clocking in correctly. Also, I'm not sure where the break room is. Could you help me find it? Thank you so much.

writing_tasks.prompt: Write 5 sentences about what you would do on your first day at a new job. Use phrases like: 'I would arrive early', 'I would ask questions', 'I would be polite'.
writing_tasks.example: On my first day, I would arrive 10 minutes early. I would introduce myself to my supervisor and coworkers. I would ask questions if I don't understand something. I would pay attention during training. I would be polite and respectful to everyone.

writing_tasks.prompt: You received this message from your supervisor: 'Your shift tomorrow is 7 AM to 3 PM. Please wear your uniform and bring your badge.' Write a polite response confirming you understand. (Write at least 3 sentences)
writing_tasks.example: Thank you for the information. I understand my shift is from 7 AM to 3 PM tomorrow. I will wear my uniform and bring my badge. I will arrive a few minutes early. See you tomorrow.

grammar_focus.title: Polite Requests with 'Could you'
grammar_focus.explanation: 'Could you...?' is very polite. Use it to ask for help at work. More polite than 'Can you...?'
examples: Could you help me? (very polite)
Can you help me? (okay, less polite)
Help me. (too direct, rude at work)
Could you show me the break room? (correct)
Could you explain this again? (correct)

practice.sentence: ___ you show me how to use this?
___ you help me with this task?
___ you tell me where the restroom is?

grammar_focus.title: Present Simple for Job Duties
grammar_focus.explanation: Use present simple (I work, I am, I do) to describe what you do regularly at work.
examples: I work from 8 AM to 5 PM. (my regular schedule)
I load trucks every day. (regular duty)
My shift starts at 7 AM. (regular time)
I take a break at noon. (regular habit)

grammar_focus.title: Imperatives for Instructions
grammar_focus.explanation: Supervisors use commands (imperatives) to give instructions. Start with the base verb.
examples: Clock in when you arrive. (command)
Wear your safety gear. (command)
Ask questions if you need help. (command)
Don't use equipment without training. (negative command)

cultural_notes: In U.S. workplaces, asking questions is encouraged. Supervisors prefer that you ask rather than make mistakes.
Being on time (or a few minutes early) is very important in American work culture.
Most jobs have a probation period (30-90 days) where they evaluate if you're a good fit.
Overtime pay is usually 1.5x your normal rate for hours over 40 per week.
Always follow safety rules. Employers are legally required to provide a safe workplace.
It's common to address supervisors by their first name (like 'Tony') unless they ask you to use a title.
